newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia overnight rate at 7.0 pct in volatile mkt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia overnight rate at 7.0 pct in volatile mkt.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was at 7.0 percent just before closing after a volatile session which saw it touching a high of 8.0 percent, dealers said.
They said the overnight rate was maintained between 7.5 and 8.0 percent for most of the session by some large banks despite liquidity remaining high. It closed at around 8.0 percent on Tuesday.
Interbank liquidity has been on the rise this week due to overseas fund inflows on the back of a strengthening ringgit.
This has pulled down most interbank rates by about 15 basis points.
"We really don't know why the overnight is so volatile. There are several rumours floating around, but no reason is known yet," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

Dealers said Bank Negara, perturbed by the inflows, may have sought the help of some large local banks to keep up interest rates. It may have also come in directly to select banks to borrow money, they said.
No confirmation could be obtained from Bank Negara.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the market to keep liquidity under check or set interest rates. Sometimes it comes in to borrow directly from select banks, which are also its principal dealers.
Some other dealers said there may not have been any intervention because the overnight came down later.
"It is possible that it was just a temporary aberration caused by the presence of some high-risk names," one dealer said.
Finance companies and merchant banks are considered higher risk borrowers in the Malaysian market.
Dealers said the bullish trend in the bond market was also halted on Wednesday, mainly due to rumours that Bank Negara was cutting down banks' liquid asset requirement.
Government bonds, Cagamas notes and bonds and other Bank Negara issues qualify for liquid assets, in which banks have to maintain 17 percent of their deposits and insurance companies 25 percent.
"The rumour is that liquid asset requirement may be reduced by two percentage points for insurance companies," a dealer said.
This will reduce the demand for instruments which qualify as liquid assets, he siad.
The 10-year government bond issued last year fell to 100.55/65 ringgit from 100.80 on Tuesday.
Earlier, other interbank rates were slightly easier as foreign funds coming in through swaps dominated the market.
They said pressure from liquidity generated by overseas funds was expected to further pressure rates following the ringgit's sharp gains in the last three days.
One-week interbank rate was expected to be around 6.80/90 percent against 6.90/7.00 previously, two-week was steady at 7.00/10 and three-week was unchanged at 7.10/20.
One-month money at 7.20/25 percent, three-month at 7.27/30 and six-month at 7.32/35, were three to five basis points lower than their previous levels.
- Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911) .
